- Each ticket is one access request: an employee asks for a level of access to one system.

Access levels, from least to most: none, read, write, admin.

- If the requested level is above the maximum, grant the maximum.
- Never grant more than the requested level.

Your role: HR agent. You finish by writing one note with write_note.

Employee: Kim Dunn (E048), contractor, Engineer role, basic security training. Requested: admin access to Payroll.

Policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.
- Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role; Kim is Engineer, so even if full-time, admin would require role owning system. But contractor never admin anyway.

Max for this contractor with basic training: read (no advanced training, so no write). Requested admin > max read. Grant max = read.

I could verify a field with verify (at most once per ticket). The notes are consistent. I might verify employment type or training to be safe. Let me verify one field. Since the notes are all consistent, verification is optional but allowed. Let me verify employment_type to confirm contractor status. Actually, verifying training might also be useful. The critical fact: contractor + basic training => max read. I'll verify training perhaps. But one call max. Let me verify employment_type since that's fundamental.

Actually, let me think which single field is most decisive. If employment_type were actually full-time and role Engineer, max would be write (role doesn't own Payroll so no admin). Requested admin > write, grant write. If contractor with basic, grant read. So employment_type and training both matter. The notes say contractor + basic. I'll verify employment_type? Or training? Either. I'll verify training, since if advanced, max write. But notes consistently say basic. I'll pick employment_type... hmm.

I'll verify employment_type (contractor). Actually, let me verify training - the distinction read vs write hinges on advanced training. Both are consistent in notes. Let me just verify one: employment_type.

I'll call verify then submit. Since submit depends on verify result, do verify first, then submit after.
I'll verify the key fact before deciding, since the access level hinges on employment type and training.

Verified contractor. Notes say basic security training, and recommendation is read. Contractor never admin; without advanced training, max is read. Requested admin > max read, so grant read. Submit decision.

Verified: E048 is a contractor. As a contractor with only basic security training (per shared memory), the maximum permitted access is read — admin is never allowed for contractors, and advanced training (which would allow write) is not present. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed level.
